success_patterns: Audit probability refinements separately: almost-sure convergence to one of a finite list does not imply that every listed limit has positive probability, and joint claims about eventual path residence and convergence need their own support.
For strict local inequalities on a trapezoidal sequence, check triples wholly inside a plateau, where equality may occur; distinguish plateau interiors from endpoints and indices outside the plateau.

When an option claims the strongest or complete result, verify each added clause independently: a valid but weaker option may be incomplete, while one unsupported extra clause invalidates a stronger composite option.

patch.reasoning: The existing skill already emphasizes exact quantifiers, equality conditions, and comparison of stronger claims. These trajectories highlight useful operational checks not stated explicitly: separate almost-sure classification from per-outcome positive-probability claims, inspect local triples in flat regions before asserting strictness, and audit every clause in a supposedly strongest or complete option.

edits.content:
- In a probabilistic classification, distinguish “the limit almost surely belongs to this finite list” from “each listed limit occurs with positive probability.” Treat per-index probability claims and joint claims such as eventual residence in a region together with convergence as separate assertions requiring support.
- For strict local inequalities on a trapezoidal or unimodal sequence, inspect triples wholly inside a constant plateau: equality may occur there even when the global shape claim holds. Track plateau interiors and endpoints separately, and assert strictness only on the indices actually covered by the result.
- When asked for the strongest or complete statement, check every added clause independently. A weaker true option may omit a valid refinement; conversely, one unsupported extra clause makes a stronger composite option incorrect.
